# Story 8.1: Unit tests for numeric column right-alignment in dms-base-table

Status: ready-for-dev

## Story

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting that `dms-base-table` body cells for numeric columns (`type: 'number' | 'currency'`) are right-aligned while non-numeric columns stay left-aligned,
So that Story 8.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it adds the type-derived alignment class and CSS.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A unit test renders `BaseTableComponent` with a column set containing at least one `type: 'number'` column (e.g. `{ field: 'qty', header: 'Qty', type: 'number' }`) and one `type: 'currency'` column, plus a `type: 'text'`/default column and a `type: 'date'` column; it asserts the rendered `<mat-cell>` for each numeric-typed column carries the right-alignment class (`.dms-body-cell--numeric`) while text/date cells do not.
2. A unit test asserts the computed style of a numeric body cell resolves to right alignment (`justify-content: flex-end`, or `text-align: right` if that mechanism is chosen) and that a non-numeric body cell does NOT resolve to it — so the visual contract (numbers hug the right edge, text stays left) is locked in.
3. A unit test asserts header cells are unaffected by the change (no numeric-alignment class on `<mat-header-cell>`), preserving the existing left-aligned header convention.
4. All new assertions in this story are marked `.skip()` (`it.skip`) in code so CI stays green while the alignment is not yet implemented; every pre-existing test in `base-table.component.spec.ts` / `base-table-mat-table.spec.ts` remains unskipped and green.

## Tasks / Subtasks

- [ ] Task 1: Add red-phase tests for numeric right-alignment (AC: #1, #2)
  - [ ] 1.1 In `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.spec.ts` (or a new sibling spec in the same folder), add a test that renders `BaseTableComponent` with mixed-type columns and asserts numeric-typed `<mat-cell>` elements carry `.dms-body-cell--numeric` while text/date cells do not.
  - [ ] 1.2 Add a computed-style assertion: numeric body cell resolves to right alignment; non-numeric body cell does not.
- [ ] Task 2: Assert headers are unaffected (AC: #3)
  - [ ] 2.1 Add a test asserting `<mat-header-cell>` elements do NOT carry the numeric-alignment class for any column type.
- [ ] Task 3: Mark all new tests `.skip()` so CI stays green (AC: #4)
  - [ ] 3.1 Prefix each new `it(...)` with `.skip` and add a comment noting Story 8.2 removes the skips, confirms red, then implements until green.

## Dev Notes

- Red-phase TDD convention: this story writes failing tests marked `.skip()` in code so CI stays green; Story 8.2's FIRST task is to remove those skips, confirm they fail (red), then implement until green.
- **Current state verified on disk:** `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.html` renders each body cell as `<mat-cell class="dms-body-cell" [style.width.px]="column.width ?? DEFAULT_COLUMN_WIDTH" [attr.data-column]="column.field">` wrapping an `[ngTemplateOutlet]` of either the consumer's `cellTemplate` or the internal `#defaultCell`. The `.dms-body-cell` SCSS block (base-table.component.scss ~line 134) sets no explicit horizontal alignment, so numeric content currently inherits default left alignment.
- **Why centralize in base-table:** every table surface (global-universe, global-screener, open-positions, sold-positions, dividend-deposits) renders through this one component; most pass a custom `#cellTemplate`, so per-template fixes would be duplicated 5× and easy to miss. A class on the shared `<mat-cell>` wrapper covers all of them at once.
- **Alignment mechanism (recommended):** make the numeric cell a flex container — `.dms-body-cell--numeric { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; align-items: center; }` — because it right-aligns *all* content types uniformly (plain `{{ }}` text, currency spans, and `<dms-editable-cell>` inputs alike). A plain `text-align: right` would NOT move block-level children like the editable-cell input. The unit test should assert the observable outcome (content at the right edge / class present) rather than over-constraining the exact CSS property, so Story 8.2 may choose flex or text-align.
- **Scope of "numeric":** `column.type === 'number' || column.type === 'currency'`. Verified numeric columns that this will cover: Universe (`distribution`, `distributions_per_year`, `yield_percent`, `avg_purchase_yield_percent`, `last_price` [currency], `most_recent_sell_price` [currency], `position`); Open Positions (`buy`/`sell` [currency, editable], `quantity`, `expectedYield`, `lastPrice`, `unrealizedGainPercent`, `unrealizedGain`, `targetGain`, `targetSell`); Sold Positions (`buy`/`sell` [currency, editable], `quantity`, `capitalGain` [currency], `capitalGainPercentage`); Dividend Deposits (amount [currency]).
- **Prose note:** the Epic prose says numeric columns "should be right aligned on decimal point where the column is a float rather than an integer." True per-decimal-point alignment requires monospace/tabular figures; the standard, maintainable interpretation is right-alignment of the cell content to its right edge (which aligns integers and floats consistently). Story 8.2 implements right-edge alignment; if Dave later wants tabular-figure decimal alignment, that is a follow-up.

### Project Structure Notes

- Add: new `it` blocks in `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.spec.ts` (or a new sibling spec file in the same folder). No production code changes in this story.
- No conflict: pure test scaffold; it does not modify the component template or SCSS.
